claims.text: Adding the MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override switches clients() to ClientPermissionsV2, whose canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException; with token-exchange and admin-fine-grained-authz:v2 both enabled, a token exchange to another audience client returns an uncaught RuntimeException (HTTP 500) instead of 403 or success.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
Label 'area/ci' could not be found and needs to be created before Dependabot can use it
Potential NullPointerException when all-clients resource is missing - getResourceTypeResource can return null and the result is passed directly to findByResource without a null guard

hasPermission(String) fetches the all-clients resource with resourceStore.findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) while hasPermission(ClientModel, String) goes through AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource — the schema entry point that UserPermissionsV2 uses — so the two paths are inconsistent.

ClientPermissionsV2 is declared public with a public constructor while its counterpart UserPermissionsV2 and its parent ClientPermissions are package-private and its only creator lives in the same package, needlessly widening the API surface.

How does an existing realm that already enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 obtain the new Clients resource and the configure / map-roles-client-scope / map-roles-composite scopes after upgrading, given that AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists?

Test uses getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) without asserting the list has at least 2 elements, which can make it flaky if the default client-scope set changes. Consider asserting a minimum size (or selecting a scope deterministically) before indexing.

ClientPermissionsV2 carries dead code copied from ClientPermissions: the never-called private getEvaluationContext method, an unused logger field, and unused imports (Scope, the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE, ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext).

ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission is missing the permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()) guard that UserPermissionsV2 added deliberately to fix an over-granting bug, so the two nearly identical evaluators differ on a security-relevant filter with no explanation.
Dead code: getEvaluationContext is never called - this private method is defined but has no callers within ClientPermissionsV2

The new CLIENTS resource type has no matching branch in AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(), so Clients permissions fall through to resource.getDisplayName() which is null, and the admin console shows null instead of 'All clients' or the clientId.
Prefer List.of() over Arrays.asList() for single-element immutable lists in ClientPermissionsV2

The all-clients fallback in hasPermission passes the result of getResourceTypeResource, which can be null, straight into PolicyStore.findByResource whose javadoc states the resource cannot be null; the JPA implementation calls resource.getId() and NPEs. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change hit this path on every canManage/canView call.
Same IndexOutOfBoundsException risk with defaultClientScopes.get(1) access without verifying the list size

PermissionClientTest mutates realm state shared across the class (renames myclient, moves a default client scope to optional, creates two client roles) without restoring it, although the same diff already uses realm.cleanup().add(...) elsewhere; this makes the tests order-dependent.
Add CLIENTS branch to getResourceName method in AdminPermissionsSchema for display name consistency with USERS pattern

AdminPermissions.registerListener was reindented and had casts respaced in the same commit, so the block reads as a full rewrite in the diff while the only behaviour change is the new outer Profile check — the one line reviewers most need to see.

Two newly added javadocs describe void require methods as 'Returns true if ... returns true' (requireView and requireViewClientScopes), while every other require* method in the same file is documented as throwing ForbiddenException when the check fails.
Javadoc for requireView() incorrectly states 'Returns {@code true}' but requireView() is a void method that throws ForbiddenException - this is a copy-paste error

Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

When a client already has its own Resource, can permissions attached to other objects but sharing the same scope be counted in its evaluation, since the FGAP schema flattens all resource types onto one shared scope set and DefaultPolicyEvaluator also queries policies by scope with a null resource?
Potential IndexOutOfBoundsException when accessing clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) assuming at least two default client scopes exist
AdminPermissionsSchema.java:53 was a blank line and is now four spaces of trailing whitespace, unrelated to what this change is doing.

The same scope-matching loop after evaluatePermission is repeated in three methods of ClientPermissionsV2 (hasPermission(ClientModel, String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String)), past the rule of three.
Client resources are added but getResourceName() has no CLIENTS case, so these resources resolve to a null label instead of a client name
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

Two of those methods build List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope) and then call contains() even though the parameter is a single scope; it is leftover from the varargs version in UserPermissionsV2 and the third method simply uses scope.equals(s).
